An '≈' target is not a deterministic assertion — a test must assert a concrete comparison (e.g. >= a floor)
findings.finding: The corpus-coverage acceptance criterion asserts approximate percentages ('≈68% of bodies / ≈78% of chars') without a deterministic numeric bound, so test_dc_corpus_coverage has no unambiguous pass/fail threshold.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, 5th bullet ('rich output for ≈68% of bodies / ≈78% of chars'); Testing 'Corpus coverage/safety'
scenarios: Renderer changes drop coverage to 60% — does the test fail? Undefined without a stated floor.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '≈68%/≈78%' with concrete floors the test asserts (e.g. `assert bodies_rich/total >= 0.65` and `chars_rich/total >= 0.75`), and define 'rich body' = at least one unit rendered (not full passthrough).

findings.finding: The plan adds pypandoc-binary as a dependency for a module living inside the reconciler package (adapters/jira_family/), but the repo invariant is that the reconciler engine is deliberately stdlib-only (pyproject.toml lines 60-61: 'the engine core and the reconciler remains stdlib-only'; dependencies=[]) with every optional dependency quarantined behind a NAMED optional-dependencies extra and imported LAZILY so `import rebar` stays dependency-free (mcp/reviewbot/ui/agents extras; ADR 0007, ADR 0059). The plan mentions a pypandoc-binary 'extra' in one Scope bullet but does not name the extra, place the renderer's pypandoc import as lazy/guarded, nor confirm the reconciler stays importable when the extra is absent.
findings.location: Approach → 'pandoc delivery (portability)'; Scope bullet 'pyproject.toml — pinned pypandoc-binary extra'
scenarios: `import rebar` or importing the reconciler in an environment without the pypandoc-binary extra installed
CI/prod resolves that omit the extra
findings.suggested_fix: Add a named extra (e.g. `wiki = ["pypandoc-binary>=..."]`) under [project.optional-dependencies] and state in the plan that render_markdown_to_wiki performs its pypandoc import lazily inside the availability probe, returning the identity passthrough (already the plan's fallback) when the import fails — so the reconciler remains importable and stdlib-only without the extra.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify HOW the code-aware arrow substitution detects code regions in raw Markdown before pandoc (fenced ```/~~~ blocks, indented code blocks, and inline backtick spans) so AC #2's '0 code-arrow rewrites over 179 bodies' has a defined mechanism, not implementer guesswork.
evidence: Plan: 'code-aware arrow substitution (`-> <- <-> =>` → `→ ← ↔ ⇒`, prose-only, skipping fenced/inline code) which MUST run on the Markdown before pandoc'
AC #2 requires 'touches 0 code arrows ... (regression over the 179 known code-arrow bodies ...: 0 rewrites)'
ABSENCE: the plan names the ordering constraint (before pandoc) but not the code-region detection method, which is what actually makes the substitution code-aware on raw Markdown
findings.finding: The code-aware arrow substitution is the load-bearing mechanism behind AC #2 (0 code-arrow rewrites over 179 bodies), yet the plan specifies it runs on 'the Markdown before pandoc' and 'skips fenced/inline code' without stating HOW code regions are detected in raw Markdown text — fenced (```/~~~) blocks, indented (4-space) code blocks, and inline backtick spans each require distinct pre-parse detection, and a naive regex over the whole body risks either rewriting arrows inside code or missing prose arrows adjacent to code.
findings.location: Approach (pure renderer module) — 'code-aware arrow substitution ... which MUST run on the Markdown before pandoc'; AC #2
scenarios: An inline code span `obj->method()` on the same line as prose containing a genuine `->`
An indented (4-space) code block that pandoc treats as code but a line-oriented arrow pass does not
A fenced block using ~~~ rather than ``` fences
findings.suggested_fix: State that arrow substitution operates on the already-segmented units and is applied only to paragraph/heading/quote units (never code units), and within those masks inline backtick spans before substituting — i.e. reuse the segmenter's own code/prose classification rather than a whole-body regex.

findings.finding: The plan depends on pandoc's `jira` writer (`-t jira`), the `commonmark` reader (`-f commonmark`), and `--wrap=none`, but pins only the `pypandoc-binary` package with no minimum pandoc VERSION floor guaranteeing those surfaces exist in the bundled binary — the `jira` writer was added at a specific pandoc release, and pypandoc-binary bundles one fixed pandoc version.
findings.location: Approach → 'pandoc delivery (portability)'; Scope bullet 'pyproject.toml — pinned pypandoc-binary extra'; AC #4
scenarios: The pinned pypandoc-binary resolves to a pandoc build predating or lacking the `jira` writer → `-t jira` errors → renderer silently falls back to identity for EVERY body.
